title: A shared ChatGPT link could read private chats. OpenAI has closed it
friendlyTitle: A shared ChatGPT link could read private chats. OpenAI has fixed it
summary: Parameter says that in October it found a way for a public ChatGPT share to run code inside the signed-in session of whoever opened it. The code could list that person's conversations and read a private chat that had never been shared. The person did not need to install an app or paste anything. OpenAI fixed the issue on 26 October and rated it P1, a high-severity report.
friendlySummary: In October, researchers at Parameter found that a public ChatGPT link could run code inside the account of the person who opened it. That code could list their chats and read a private one that had never been shared. They did not need to install anything. OpenAI fixed it on 26 October and marked it as a serious bug.
whyItMatters: This is a closed hole, not an open one. If you open a shared ChatGPT link today, this particular path should not reach your private chats. The useful habit remains: treat an unexpected share the way you treat an unexpected attachment. Parameter's write-up is a postmortem of a fixed bug, not a current way in.
